grafenberg.description:
Kinetic Distro is an independent music label and creative distribution platform dedicated to pushing the boundaries of sound, identity, and artistic storytelling in the digital age.

Built on a vision of movement and transformation, Kinetic Distro operates at the intersection of genres, cultures, and eras—curating a diverse roster of artists who each embody a distinct sonic universe. From cinematic electronic landscapes to hypnotic techno, neo-soul narratives, experimental pop, and heavy sonic architectures, the label thrives on contrast, evolution, and cohesion.

The roster includes projects such as Grafenberg, Broken Shaman, Chromabone, Nosfera Disco Club, VEIN//Mirror, Iron Covenant, Anatolian Mirage, and Lykke—each representing a unique dimension of the Kinetic Distro ecosystem. Rather than following trends, the label builds immersive worlds, where every release contributes to a larger, interconnected artistic continuum.

Kinetic Distro is not just a distributor—it is a creative engine. Through meticulous curation, visual identity development, and narrative-driven releases, the label transforms music into experiences. Each project is approached as a living entity, evolving across albums, concepts, and aesthetic directions.

Driven by independence and a commitment to artistic integrity, Kinetic Distro embraces modern production tools, global influences, and a release strategy designed for the streaming era—while maintaining a strong emphasis on authenticity and long-term vision.

At its core, Kinetic Distro is about momentum: sound in motion, ideas in evolution, and artists in constant transformation.

broken-shaman.description:
Broken Shaman works in the space where ritual replaces meaning.
Groove is used as pressure, voice as initiation, silence as law.
Nothing is explained. Everything is felt.

This is music for bodies before belief,
for desire before language,
for those who listen after the signal is gone.

The ritual never ended.
It only changed form.

iron-covenant.description:
“The Big Four were never four.”

Forged on the industrial East Coast, somewhere between rusted docks and dim basement clubs, Iron Covenant emerged in the early 80s with a paradoxical identity:
East Coast attitude. West Coast precision.

While Anthrax was shaking New York and the Californian scene was defining thrash metal’s future, Iron Covenant quietly carved its own path — blending surgical riff discipline, relentless rhythmic force, and unforgettable hooks.

Too technical to be just another thrash band.
Too raw and uncompromising to become mainstream.

They never chased the crown.
Eventually, it found them.

🧬 The Core Line-up

Jack “Razor” Haldane – vocals / rhythm guitar
Charismatic frontman with a voice balancing grit and melody.

Ethan Cross – lead guitar
Riff architect and obsessive craftsman of structure and detail.

Marko Vega – bass
Dark groove foundation, occasionally hinting at blues and funk influences.

Caleb North – drums
Precision machine. Metronomic power with surgical timing.

Remarkably, the band maintained nearly the same line-up for over three decades, a rare stability that helped shape its unmistakable sound.

vein-mirror.description:
VEIN//MIRROR is a dark, sensual and cinematic ritual of sound.
Born at the intersection of analog warmth and poetic violence, the project explores the fragile space where desire turns toxic and beauty becomes dangerous.

Driven by hypnotic rhythms, melancholic guitars, saturated Moog pulses, Mellotron choirs and deep, intimate vocals, VEIN//MIRROR creates immersive soundscapes that feel both ancient and futuristic. Each track unfolds like a fractured reflection — emotional, physical, and deeply immersive — where intimacy and brutality coexist.

Love and Venom Taste the Same, the debut album, is a journey through sensual decay, ritualistic tension and sacred collapse. A collection of cinematic scenes where love is never innocent, salvation is forged through sacrifice, and every breath carries the taste of poison.

VEIN//MIRROR is not a genre.
It is a ceremony, a wound, a mirror.
Music for those who seek the sacred in the forbidden — and the forbidden in the sacred.
